name: relative-time-card

frames.best_why: The hover card is fully open with all four timezone rows readable over the activity list.

tagline: Hover a timestamp to see the exact time in several zones.
summary: Activity rows each end in a live relative time such as one hour ago. Hovering one opens a card with the precise date and time in New York, London, Tokyo and the local offset.
appearance: A bordered dark list of four activity rows, each pairing a name and action on the left with a muted absolute timestamp on the right, above a View time details button. On hover a dark card floats over the list showing a relative line and four timezone rows tagged with small grey chips.
behaviour: Hovering or focusing a timestamp opens the card after a short delay with the relative age and the exact time in each configured zone; moving away closes it. The ago label refreshes on a timer while the page is mounted.
demo_content: Team activity from Maya Chen, Leo Park, Ana Ruiz and Release bot with November 2026 timestamps.
search_phrases: hover a timestamp to see the exact time
how long ago was this posted
time in multiple timezones on hover
date tooltip for activity feed rows
world clock popover for a timestamp
exact time with offset for remote teams
tooltip showing the date in other cities
use_when: An activity feed for a distributed team needs exact times and several zones without leaving the page.
avoid_when: It opens on hover with a delay, and the narrow card crowds long zone names and timestamps together.
customise: Pass date and a timezones array, pick a variant, and pass children to replace the trigger label. openDelay, closeDelay, updateInterval and the hover-card side and alignment are props too.
weight_why: One timestamp plus an interval that recomputes the relative label every second.

a11y.note: The trigger is a real button with a focus ring and each zone row is labelled, but the card never checks reduced-motion settings.

issues: The hover card covers the activity rows it belongs to, hiding the action text and other timestamps while open.
The timezone rows are cramped, and the last zone chip is so dim on the dark card that it is barely readable.
polish_why: Tidy activity list and a useful zone card; the popover covers the list and its rows are cramped.
title: Relative Time Card
